newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt pare losses to end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt pare losses to end mixed.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices pared losses late Wednesday to end a volatile session mixed as market participants saw good buying opportunities in the wake of a sharp selloff over the past week, trading sources said.

"We have been all over the place. I haven't seen the market like this since last year at this time. Yesterday we had panic selling, today we had panic buying," said a head trader at a major U.S. investment bank.

Relief that Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony was over and did not bring any surprises added to the positive tone in the U.S. financial markets and, in turn, helped bolster emerging market debt.
Greenspan, who tesified before the House Banking Monetary Policy subcommittee, said among other things that if profit margins rise as expected stocks were properly priced.
The Fed Chairman also said that the U.S. economy was running close to capacity but was not overheating.
